deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics and is not by Riemann. It is a fair copy, in a calligraphic hand unlike Riemann's, of an announcement in the Comptes Rendus of the Paris Académie des Sciences dated 14 June 1869, p. 1409. That is about three years after Riemann's death in July 1866.

The announcement concerns the Grand Prix de Mathématiques to be awarded in 1871:
- The 1867 question was 'Apporter un progrès notable dans la théorie des surfaces algébriques' (make notable progress in the theory of algebraic surfaces).
- Only one memoir was submitted, and the commission judged that the prize should not be awarded.
- The commission members were Serret, Liouville, Chasles, Hermite, and Ossian Bonnet as rapporteur.
- The Academy withdrew that question. It substituted a study of the equations for determining the singular moduli, those for which the transformation formula of elliptic functions leads to complex multiplication. In modern terms these are the modular and class equations for CM values of the modulus k (or of j).
- The prize is a gold medal worth 3000 francs. Entries are due at the Secrétariat de l'Institut before 1 June 1871.

The previous folio copies the general competition conditions from p. 1423 of the same volume. These include no return of manuscripts and a common closing date of 1 June, fixed in 1865.

The pages most plausibly belong to a posthumous dossier on Paris prize competitions, assembled by the editors or the family. Riemann's own Paris entry was the 1861 heat-conduction essay ('Commentatio mathematica...'), which explains the bundle title 'Waermeleitung'.

There is no derivation to reconstruct. The only mathematical content is the prize question on singular moduli and complex multiplication. That topic was associated with Abel, Kronecker, Hermite and later Weber.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page is an administrative copy.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a posthumous copy of a published 1869 Comptes Rendus prize announcement in another hand. It contains no mathematics by Riemann. Its only interest is archival: it shows how the Nachlass bundle was assembled around the Paris prize.

transcription_corrections: The left-margin fragments ('o', 'e', 'u.') bleed through from the facing page and are not part of this text.
The pencil numeral '47' at the right margin is the folio number. The 'next page' transcription '46' is likewise just a folio number.
The image spells 'Sécrétariat' (with accent) on the previous page; on this page it reads 'Sécrétariat de l'In-stitut', and the machine 'Secrétariat' is a normalization.
'Serret' is written with a looped S that resembles 'Lerret'; the reading Serret is correct.
The line 'Le prix qui consistera...' has 'trois mille francs' underlined in the original.
